ground_truth_text: Immediate coronary angiography with percutaneous coronary intervention
question_with_options:
A 58-year-old man with hypertension has 45 minutes of crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm. He is diaphoretic, and ECG shows ST-segment elevations in leads II, III, and aVF. Which of the following is the best next step in management?
(A) Oral omeprazole and outpatient follow-up
(B) Immediate coronary angiography with percutaneous coronary intervention
(C) Inhaled albuterol and systemic corticosteroids
(D) High-dose amoxicillin for otitis media
(E) Reassurance and discharge home
